newsitem.title: USA: TWO COMPANIES CUT WORKERS DUE TO UPS STRIKE.
newsitem.headline: TWO COMPANIES CUT WORKERS DUE TO UPS STRIKE.

text.p: Two companies said they laid off workers because of the United Parcel Service strike -- Russ Berrie and Co. Inc., a maker of plush dolls and gift items, and National TechTeam Inc., a provider of data services.
Russ Berrie, based in New Jersey, said Wednesday it cut 100 part-time and temporary workers because the strike has reduced its ability to ship goods.

"At this time of year, we're shipping a lot of seasonal and Christmas items. We can't find enough sources to get out the products," President Curts Cooke said. "We're getting out about 20 to 30 percent of our normal shipments."
If the UPS strike ends, the employees laid off Friday probably would be rehired, Cooke said. The size of the company's work force was not immediately available.
National TechTeam, based in Dearborn, Mich., said it laid off UPS support agents who service hardware and software placed at customer locations by UPS.
The company said in a statement issued late Tuesday that it laid off the agents at UPS' request but did not say how many. Company officials were not available for comment.
The strike by 185,000 Teamsters at UPS entered its 10th day Wednesday with no face-to-face talks scheduled between the union and the nation's largest package delivery company.
UPS normally handles 12 million packages a day, 80 percent of those shipped by ground nationwide, and many businesses are struggling to deliver goods or find alternate shippers.
UPS Chairman James Kelly said Tuesday that 15,000 Teamsters could lose their jobs if the strike lasted two weeks. Union officials dismissed the statement as a threat.
